The revised regulatory timetable delays a potential commercial launch of the treatment, which represents an important component of Vertex’s planned expansion into nephrology. Why Has the FDA Extended Its Review of Povetacicept? The FDA’s original Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date for povetacicept was 30 November 2026. The revised deadline is now no later than 28 February 2027. The extension follows an information request issued by the FDA during the latter stages of its review. Although Vertex responded promptly, the regulator classified the submission as a major amendment requiring additional assessment time. The announcement follows a period of gains for Vertex shares, which recently reached a 52-week high of $571.75. How Have Wall Street Analysts Responded to the Regulatory Delay? JPMorgan maintained its Overweight rating and $570 price target on Vertex following the announcement. While the investment bank described the postponement as disappointing, it indicated that the revised regulatory timetable had not fundamentally changed its longer-term investment outlook. JPMorgan estimates that povetacicept could generate peak sales of $3.4 billion in the IgA nephropathy market. What Other Factors Are Investors Monitoring? A Form 144 notice relating to a proposed insider share sale was filed on 26 November. Recent insider transaction data also showed 12 open-market sales and no purchases over the preceding six months. Meanwhile, shares of competing drugmaker Vera Therapeutics rose sharply in after-hours trading following news of the regulatory extension. Vera already markets TRUTAKNA for IgA nephropathy, and the postponed FDA decision on povetacicept extends the period before Vertex could potentially enter the market. What Does the Regulatory Delay Mean for Vertex’s Growth Strategy? Povetacicept represents a central component of Vertex’s plans to establish nephrology as its fifth commercial franchise.
